claim: Mycobacterium tuberculosis virulent strain H37Rv (Rv) causes double strand breaks (DSBs) in host cells
source: The virulent Mtb strain, Rv caused double strand breaks (DSBs), whereas the non-virulent Ra strain triggered single-stranded DNA generation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that Rv causes DSBs, and this is supported by experimental data showing γH2AX induction and ATM-Chk2 pathway activation in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Mycobacterium tuberculosis non-virulent strain H37Ra (Ra) triggers single-stranded DNA generation in host cells
source: The virulent Mtb strain, Rv caused double strand breaks (DSBs), whereas the non-virulent Ra strain triggered single-stranded DNA generation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this, and Figure 2b-c shows ATR-Chk1 pathway activation and RPA2 foci formation upon Ra infection.

claim: SecA2 secretome effectors are essential and adequate for the genesis of DSBs in host cells
source: The effectors secreted by SecA2 pathway were essential and adequate for the genesis of DSBs.
evidence: The abstract states this explicitly, and Figure 4 shows that RvΔsecA2 mutant and its culture filtrate fail to induce γH2AX, while Rv and RvΔRD1 do.

claim: Mtb infection activates ATM-Chk2 pathway of DNA damage response signaling
source: Accumulation of DSBs mediated through Rv activates ATM-Chk2 pathway of DNA damage response (DDR) signaling, resulting in altered cell cycle.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this, and Figure 2b shows phosphorylation of ATM and Chk2 upon Rv infection.

claim: Mtb gains survival advantage through ATM-Akt signaling cascade instead of classical ATM-Chk2 DDR
source: Instead of the classical ATM-Chk2 DDR, Mtb gains survival advantage through ATM-Akt signaling cascade.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this, and Figures 5 and 6 show that ATM inhibition reduces Mtb survival while Chk2 inhibition does not, and that Akt is activated downstream of ATM.

claim: In vivo infection with Mtb leads to sustained DSBs and ATM activation during chronic phase of tuberculosis
source: Notably, in vivo infection with Mtb led to sustained DSBs and ATM activation during chronic phase of tuberculosis.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this, and Figure 7a-b shows elevated γH2AX and pATM levels in lungs and spleen of mice at 56 days post-infection.

claim: Addition of ATM inhibitor enhances isoniazid mediated Mtb clearance in macrophages
source: Addition of ATM inhibitor enhances isoniazid mediated Mtb clearance in macrophages as well as in murine infection model, suggesting its utility for host directed adjunct therapy.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this, and Figure 7c shows that ATM-I + INH treatment results in better clearance than INH alone in macrophages.

claim: Addition of ATM inhibitor enhances isoniazid mediated Mtb clearance in murine infection model
source: Addition of ATM inhibitor enhances isoniazid mediated Mtb clearance in macrophages as well as in murine infection model, suggesting its utility for host directed adjunct therapy.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this, and Figure 7e-f shows that ATM-I + INH treatment results in ~1 log fold better clearance than INH alone in mouse lungs and spleen.

claim: ATM is activated through autophosphorylation of S1981 residue
source: ATM is activated through autophosphorylation of S1981 residue and is subsequently recruited to the double strand breaks (DSBs) through a sensor complex, MRN (MRE11, NBS1 and Rad50) (Lee and Paull, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to Lee and Paull, 2005, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: ATM is recruited to double strand breaks through MRN sensor complex (MRE11, NBS1 and Rad50)
source: ATM is activated through autophosphorylation of S1981 residue and is subsequently recruited to the double strand breaks (DSBs) through a sensor complex, MRN (MRE11, NBS1 and Rad50) (Lee and Paull, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to Lee and Paull, 2005, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: DNA-PKcs is recruited to DSBs through DSB-bound heterodimer Ku70-80
source: DSBs are also the site of recruitment and activation of DNA-PKcs, facilitated by a DSB-bound heterodimer Ku70-80 (Gottlieb and Jackson, 1993; Spagnolo et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to Gottlieb and Jackson, 1993 and Spagnolo et al., 2006, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: ATR-ATRIP complex is recruited in response to RPA-coated ssDNA
source: ATR-ATRIP complex is recruited in response to RPA-coated ssDNA (Ball et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to Ball et al., 2005, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: Phosphorylation of H2AX at serine 139 (γH2AX) is a marker for DNA damage
source: Phosphorylation of H2AX at the serine 139 (termed γH2AX), at the chromatin regions flanking the damage site is considered as a marker for DNA damage (Burma et al., 2001; Rogakou et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to Burma et al., 2001 and Rogakou et al., 1998, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: Phosphorylation of H2AX is predominantly modulated by ATM, with ATR and DNA-PKcs also contributing
source: While phosphorylation of H2AX is predominantly modulated by ATM, ATR and DNA-PKcs also contribute either partially or entirely (Burma et al., 2001; Royo et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to Burma et al., 2001, Royo et al., 2013, and Wang et al., 2005, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: Pathogenic Escherichia coli and Helicobacter pylori are capable of imparting notable DNA damage to the host and subsequently impair the DDR to avoid premature cell death
source: Pathogenic Escherichia coli and Helicobacter pylori are capable of imparting notable DNA damage to the host and subsequently impair the DDR to avoid premature cell death (Cuevas-Ramos et al., 2010; Toller et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to Cuevas-Ramos et al., 2010 and Toller et al., 2011.

claim: Chlamydia trachomatis triggers DSBs and γH2AX induction but impairs DDR by inhibiting recruitment of 53BP1
source: Chlamydia trachomatis triggers DSBs in the host, and γH2AX induction but simultaneously it impairs the DDR by inhibiting the recruitment of 53BP1, ensuing inadequate signal amplification (Chumduri et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to Chumduri et al., 2013.

claim: Listeriolysin O (LLO) secreted by Listeria monocytogenes induces degradation of MRE11
source: Listeriolysin O (LLO) secreted by Listeria monocytogenes induces degradation of crucial DNA damage sensor, MRE11. This results in impaired DDR, curtailing the host ability to halt cell cycle, thus successfully promoting multiplication and survival of the pathogen (Samba-Louaka et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to Samba-Louaka et al., 2014.

claim: H. pylori impedes nucleotide repair by downregulating proteins and transcripts involved in mismatch and base excision repair
source: H. pylori impedes nucleotide repair by downregulating the proteins and their respective transcripts that are involved in mismatch and base excision repair (Kim et al., 2002; Machado et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to Kim et al., 2002 and Machado et al., 2009.

claim: Neisseria gonorrhoeae, H. pylori and C. trachomatis downregulate p53 levels to promote host cell survival and inhibit apoptosis
source: Neisseria gonorrhoeae, H. pylori and C. trachomatis also downregulate p53 levels to promote host cell survival and inhibit apoptosis (Buti et al., 2011; Wei et al., 2010; Vielfort et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to Buti et al., 2011, Wei et al., 2010, and Vielfort et al., 2013.

claim: Mtb secretes effectors that modulate host cellular processes including phagosome maturation, apoptosis, autophagy, calcium homeostasis, and activation of pro-inflammatory responses
source: These effectors modulate host cellular processes such as phagosome maturation, apoptosis, autophagy, calcium homeostasis, activation of pro-inflammatory responses and TLR, TNFα, MAPK signaling pathways (Dey and Bishai, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to Dey and Bishai, 2014.

claim: PMA differentiated THP-1 cells infected with H37Rv show considerable DNA damage compared to uninfected control
source: Results showed considerable DNA damage in the infected cells compared to the corresponding uninfected control and these observations were consistent across all the three cell types (Figure 1a–c).
evidence: Figure 1a shows elevated γH2AX levels in THP-1 cells infected with Rv at multiple time points compared to uninfected controls.

claim: RAW264.7 macrophages infected with H37Rv show considerable DNA damage compared to uninfected control
source: Results showed considerable DNA damage in the infected cells compared to the corresponding uninfected control and these observations were consistent across all the three cell types (Figure 1a–c).
evidence: Figure 1b shows elevated γH2AX levels in RAW264.7 cells infected with Rv at multiple time points compared to uninfected controls.

claim: Primary murine peritoneal macrophages infected with H37Rv show considerable DNA damage compared to uninfected control
source: Results showed considerable DNA damage in the infected cells compared to the corresponding uninfected control and these observations were consistent across all the three cell types (Figure 1a–c).
evidence: Figure 1c shows elevated γH2AX levels in peritoneal macrophages infected with Rv at multiple time points compared to uninfected controls.

claim: DNA damage in host cells can be observed as early as 1 hr post Mtb infection
source: The damage could be observed as early as 1 hr post infection (p.i) (Figure 1b) and persisted even at 72 hr (Figure 1a).
evidence: Figure 1b shows γH2AX induction at 1 hr post-infection in RAW264.7 cells.

claim: DNA damage in host cells persists even at 72 hr post Mtb infection
source: The damage could be observed as early as 1 hr post infection (p.i) (Figure 1b) and persisted even at 72 hr (Figure 1a).
evidence: Figure 1a shows continued γH2AX expression at 72 hr post-infection in THP-1 cells.

claim: Only live Mtb bacilli can cause damage to the host genome, not heat-killed bacteria
source: Results showed that (Figure 1d) only the live bacilli could cause damage to the host genome.
evidence: Figure 1d shows that heat-killed Rv (HK-Rv) does not induce γH2AX while live Rv does in RAW264.7 cells.

claim: Both H37Ra and H37Rv infected THP1 cells show considerably higher γH2AX levels compared with uninfected control
source: While both Ra and Rv infected THP1 cells showed considerably higher γH2AX levels compared with the uninfected control, there was consistent and noticeably higher levels of γH2AX levels in Rv compared with the Ra infected cells (Figure 1e; compare 4, 24 and 48 hr time points).
evidence: Figure 1e shows elevated γH2AX in both Ra and Rv infected THP1 cells compared to uninfected controls.

claim: H37Rv shows consistently and noticeably higher levels of γH2AX compared with H37Ra infected THP1 cells at 4, 24 and 48 hr time points
source: While both Ra and Rv infected THP1 cells showed considerably higher γH2AX levels compared with the uninfected control, there was consistent and noticeably higher levels of γH2AX levels in Rv compared with the Ra infected cells (Figure 1e; compare 4, 24 and 48 hr time points).
evidence: Figure 1e shows higher γH2AX bands in Rv lanes compared to Ra lanes at 4, 24, and 48 hr.

claim: In RAW cells, higher γH2AX levels in H37Rv compared to H37Ra was apparent only in the early time points (up to 4 hr)
source: However, in case of RAW cells the higher γH2AX levels in Rv was apparent only in the early time points (Figure 1f and g: up to 4 hr).
evidence: Figure 1f and 1g show differential γH2AX levels between Rv and Ra at early time points in RAW cells.

claim: Significantly higher numbers of γH2AX foci are observed at both 4 and 24 hr post-infection in RAW264.7 cells compared with uninfected controls
source: We performed immunofluorescence experiments using antibodies specific for γH2AX and observed significantly higher numbers of γH2AX foci at both 4 and 24 hr p.i (Figure 1h) compared with the uninfected controls.
evidence: Figure 1h shows immunofluorescence images with γH2AX foci in Rv and Ra infected RAW264.7 cells at 4 and 24 hr, absent in uninfected controls.

claim: H37Ra infection leads to formation of distinct nuclear pRPA2 foci
source: Infection by Ra led to the formation of distinct nuclear pRPA2 (Figure 2c) and RPA2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a) foci and robust activation of ATR-Chk1 pathway (Figure 2b; right panel), suggesting that Ra induces generation of ssDNA.
evidence: Figure 2c shows immunofluorescence images with pRPA2 foci in Ra infected RAW264.7 cells.

claim: H37Ra infection leads to robust activation of ATR-Chk1 pathway
source: Infection by Ra led to the formation of distinct nuclear pRPA2 (Figure 2c) and RPA2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a) foci and robust activation of ATR-Chk1 pathway (Figure 2b; right panel), suggesting that Ra induces generation of ssDNA.
evidence: Figure 2b right panel shows phosphorylation of ATR and Chk1 in Ra infected RAW264.7 cells.

claim: H37Ra induces generation of single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) in host cells
source: Infection by Ra led to the formation of distinct nuclear pRPA2 (Figure 2c) and RPA2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a) foci and robust activation of ATR-Chk1 pathway (Figure 2b; right panel), suggesting that Ra induces generation of ssDNA.
evidence: The formation of RPA foci and ATR-Chk1 activation are indicators of ssDNA, as stated in the text and shown in Figures 2b-c.

claim: H37Rv infection leads to significant activation of ATM-Chk2 pathway in RAW and peritoneal macrophages
source: On the other hand, infection by Rv led to significant activation of ATM-Chk2 pathway in both RAW and PΦ cells, suggesting occurrence of DSBs in the host nuclei (Figure 2b, left panel and 2d).
evidence: Figure 2b left panel and 2d show phosphorylation of ATM and Chk2 in Rv infected RAW and peritoneal macrophages.

claim: H37Rv infection causes occurrence of DSBs in the host nuclei
source: On the other hand, infection by Rv led to significant activation of ATM-Chk2 pathway in both RAW and PΦ cells, suggesting occurrence of DSBs in the host nuclei (Figure 2b, left panel and 2d).
evidence: ATM-Chk2 pathway activation is indicative of DSBs, as shown in Figures 2b and 2d.

claim: Distinct pATM foci are observed upon H37Rv infection
source: These results were corroborated by immunofluorescence experiments, wherein we observed distinct pATM foci upon Rv infection (Figure 2e).
evidence: Figure 2e shows immunofluorescence images with pATM foci in Rv infected peritoneal macrophages.

claim: H37Rv infection leads to enhanced phosphorylation of Nbs1, MDC1, and 53BP1
source: While there were no significant perturbation in the protein levels, enhanced phosphorylation of Nbs1, MDC1, 53BP1, representing the activated forms, was evident upon Rv infection (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b and c; Shiloh, 2003).
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 1b and c show increased phosphorylation of these proteins in Rv infected cells.

claim: γH2AX and 53BP1 foci colocalize in H37Rv infected peritoneal macrophages
source: Distinct focal pattern and colocalization of γH2AX and 53BP1 foci in Rv infected PΦ supported the argument that infection with Rv induces DSBs (Figure 2f).
evidence: Figure 2f shows immunofluorescence images with colocalized γH2AX and 53BP1 foci in Rv infected peritoneal macrophages.

claim: Treatment of H37Rv infected cells with isoniazid (INH) leads to time dependent reduction in γH2AX, pATM and pChk2 levels
source: While γH2AX levels continued to persist in Rv infected cells, treatment of INH led to time dependent reduction in γH2AX, pATM and pChk2 levels (Figure 3c), concomitant with the clearance of the pathogen (Figure 3b).
evidence: Figure 3c shows decreased levels of γH2AX, pATM, and pChk2 in Rv+INH treated cells over time compared to Rv alone.

claim: Isoniazid treatment leads to efficient clearance of intracellular H37Rv pathogen
source: Analysis of colony-forming units (CFUs) at different time points post Rv infection ascertained efficient clearance of intracellular pathogen in the presence with INH (Figure 3b and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 3b shows reduced CFUs in Rv+INH treated cells compared to Rv alone at 24, 48, and 72 hr.

claim: Continuous generation of DSBs occurs during prolonged H37Rv infection despite active DDR
source: Thus, the data suggests that even though DDR is active, inefficient repair is due to continuous generation of DSBs during prolonged Rv infection.
evidence: This is inferred from the persistent γH2AX levels in Rv infected cells and the reduction upon INH treatment that clears the pathogen, as shown in Figures 3a-c.

claim: H37Rv infected GFP+ve population shows decreased accumulation of cells in G1 phase at 4 hr post-infection compared to uninfected cells
source: Interestingly, compared with the uninfected cell population, Rv infected GFP+ve population showed decreased accumulation of cells in G1 phase, soon after the infection (4 h p.i). Lowered accumulation of cells in the G1 phase suggest alterations in the progression of cell cycle in the cells harboring intracellular bacilli (Figure 3e).
evidence: Figure 3e shows pie charts with decreased G1 phase percentage in Rv infected cells at 4 hr compared to uninfected controls.

claim: At late stages of H37Rv infection, there is concomitant increase in the sub-G1 cell population, indicative of cell death
source: Importantly, at late stages of infection we observed concomitant increase in the sub-G1 cell population, indicative of cell death (Figure 3e).
evidence: Figure 3e shows increased sub-G1 population in Rv infected cells at 24 and 48 hr.

claim: H37Rv infection leads to elevated levels of p53 and p21
source: Elevated levels of p53 and p21 upon Rv infection are reflective of molecular level alterations in the cell cycle leading to eventual cell death indicated as sub-G1 population (Figure 3g).
evidence: Figure 3g shows increased p53 and p21 protein levels in Rv infected RAW264.7 cells at 24 and 48 hr.

claim: Addition of Mtb culture filtrate (CF) results in robust γH2AX induction, even higher than those observed upon H37Rv infection
source: Addition of Mtb CF resulted in robust γH2AX induction, even higher than those observed upon Rv infection (Figure 4b).
evidence: Figure 4b shows higher γH2AX levels in Rv-CF treated cells compared to Rv infected cells.

claim: As little as 1 µg/ml Mtb culture filtrate treatment induces significant γH2AX
source: Importantly as little as 1 µg/ml CF treatment induced significant γH2AX (Figure 4c).
evidence: Figure 4c shows γH2AX induction at 1 µg/ml Rv-CF treatment at 4, 24, and 48 hr.

claim: Host cells infected with H37Rv, RvΔRD1, or RvΔCE have comparable γH2AX levels
source: Host cells infected with Rv or RvΔRD1(Rv carrying RD1 deletion) or RvΔCE (Rv strain with CFP10-ESAT6 deletion) had comparable γH2AX levels (Figure 4d & f).
evidence: Figure 4d and 4f show similar γH2AX levels in Rv and RvΔRD1 or RvΔCE infected cells.

claim: Expression of γH2AX observed upon infection with RvΔsecA2 is significantly lower at later time points compared to H37Rv
source: On the other hand, expression of γH2AX observed upon infection with RvΔsecA2 (SecA2 exporter mutant) was significantly lower at the later time points (Figure 4e & f).
evidence: Figure 4e and 4f show reduced γH2AX levels in RvΔsecA2 infected cells at 24 and 48 hr compared to Rv.

claim: Cells treated with culture filtrate from RvΔRD1 show γH2AX levels comparable to those observed upon Rv-CF treatment
source: While the γH2AX levels in cells treated with CF from RvΔRD1 were comparable to those observed upon Rv-CF treatment; cells treated with RvΔsecA2-CF showed negligible γH2AX levels (Figure 4g).
evidence: Figure 4g shows similar γH2AX levels in Rv-CF and ΔRD1-CF treated RAW264.7 cells.

claim: Cells treated with RvΔsecA2-CF show negligible γH2AX levels
source: While the γH2AX levels in cells treated with CF from RvΔRD1 were comparable to those observed upon Rv-CF treatment; cells treated with RvΔsecA2-CF showed negligible γH2AX levels (Figure 4g).
evidence: Figure 4g shows minimal γH2AX in ΔsecA2-CF treated RAW264.7 cells compared to Rv-CF.

claim: Treatment with Rv-CF or RvΔRD1-CF leads to activation of ATM and Chk2
source: Treatment of cells either with Rv-CF or RvΔRD1-CF led to the activation of DDR players, ATM and Chk2. However, treatment with RvΔsecA2-CF cells did not show ATM-Chk2 activation.
evidence: Figure 4g shows pATM and pChk2 in Rv-CF and ΔRD1-CF treated cells but not in ΔsecA2-CF treated cells.

claim: Treatment with RvΔsecA2-CF does not show ATM-Chk2 activation
source: Treatment of cells either with Rv-CF or RvΔRD1-CF led to the activation of DDR players, ATM and Chk2. However, treatment with RvΔsecA2-CF cells did not show ATM-Chk2 activation.
evidence: Figure 4g shows absence of pATM and pChk2 in ΔsecA2-CF treated RAW264.7 cells.

claim: Effectors secreted by SecA2 pathway are necessary and sufficient for inflicting genotoxic stress in the host
source: Together, results suggest that effectors secreted by SecA2 pathway are necessary and sufficient for inflicting genotoxic stress in the host.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the data in Figure 4 showing that RvΔsecA2 mutant and its CF fail to induce DNA damage markers.

claim: Treatment of H37Rv infected cells with ATM inhibitor (ATM-I) results in substantial decrease in γH2AX levels
source: Treatment of infected cells with ATM-I inhibitor resulted in substantial decrease in the γH2AX levels and abrogation of ATM and Chk2 activation (Figure 5a).
evidence: Figure 5a shows reduced γH2AX, pATM, and pChk2 in Rv+ATM-I treated peritoneal macrophages compared to Rv alone.

claim: Treatment of H37Rv infected cells with ATM inhibitor results in abrogation of ATM and Chk2 activation
source: Treatment of infected cells with ATM-I inhibitor resulted in substantial decrease in the γH2AX levels and abrogation of ATM and Chk2 activation (Figure 5a).
evidence: Figure 5a shows loss of pATM and pChk2 in Rv+ATM-I treated cells.

claim: ATM-I treatment results in disappearance of pATM foci in H37Rv-infected cells
source: This was also reflected in disappearance of pATM foci upon ATM-I treatment in Rv-infected cells (Figure 5b).
evidence: Figure 5b shows absence of pATM foci in Rv+ATM-I treated peritoneal macrophages compared to Rv alone.

claim: ATM-I treatment of H37Rv-infected cells results in reduced survival of the pathogen in a dose dependent manner
source: Notably, ATM-I treatment of Rv-infected cells resulted in reduced survival of the pathogen in a dose dependent manner (Figure 5c and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 5c shows decreased CFUs with increasing concentrations of ATM-I (1, 5, 10 µM) in Rv infected peritoneal macrophages.

claim: ATM-I does not impact in vitro Mtb growth
source: However, ATM-I did not impact in vitro Mtb growth suggesting that the clearance of the bacilli is mediated through inhibition of ATM activation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1 shows that ATM-I does not affect Mtb viability in culture (MIC assay).

claim: Treatment of H37Rv infected cells with Chk2 inhibitor has negligible effect on Mtb survival
source: Interestingly, treatment of infected cells with Chk2 inhibitor (Chk2-I) had negligible effect on Mtb survival (Figure 5d & e; Figure 5—source data 1), suggesting that while ATM activation is essential; Mtb survival is not dependent on the activation of downstream effectors.
evidence: Figure 5e shows similar CFUs in Rv and Rv+Chk2-I treated peritoneal macrophages.

claim: Mtb survival is not dependent on the activation of Chk2, the downstream effector of ATM
source: Interestingly, treatment of infected cells with Chk2 inhibitor (Chk2-I) had negligible effect on Mtb survival (Figure 5d & e; Figure 5—source data 1), suggesting that while ATM activation is essential; Mtb survival is not dependent on the activation of downstream effectors.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effect of Chk2-I on CFUs shown in Figure 5e, despite ATM activation being essential (Figure 5c).

claim: Infection of peritoneal macrophages with H37Rv results in activation of DNA-PKcs, albeit to much lower levels and at later time points compared with ATM
source: Infection of PΦ with Rv resulted in the activation of DNA-PKcs, albeit to much lower levels and at later time points compared with the ATM (Figure 6a).
evidence: Figure 6a shows pDNA-PKcs appearing at later time points with lower intensity compared to pATM in Rv infected peritoneal macrophages.

claim: Addition of DNA-PK inhibitor to ATM inhibitor results in further decrease in γH2AX levels in H37Rv infected cells
source: While the addition of ATR-I to ATM-I did not alter the residual levels of γH2AX, addition of DNA-PK-I to ATM-I resulted in further decrease in the levels of γH2AX, corroborating data in Figure 6a.
evidence: Figure 6b shows lower γH2AX levels in ATM-I+DNA-PK-I treated cells compared to ATM-I alone.

claim: Addition of ATR inhibitor to ATM inhibitor does not alter the residual levels of γH2AX in H37Rv infected cells
source: While the addition of ATR-I to ATM-I did not alter the residual levels of γH2AX, addition of DNA-PK-I to ATM-I resulted in further decrease in the levels of γH2AX, corroborating data in Figure 6a.
evidence: Figure 6b shows similar γH2AX levels in ATM-I and ATM-I+ATR-I treated cells.

claim: Addition of DNA-PK inhibitor or ATR inhibitor alone does not alter CFUs in H37Rv infected cells
source: It is evident that addition of DNA-PK-I or ATR-I did not alter the CFUs, suggesting that even though DNA-PK seems to be activated upon Mtb infection, it does not influence the survival of the pathogen (Figure 6c and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 6c shows similar CFUs in Rv, Rv+DNA-PK-I, and Rv+ATR-I treated peritoneal macrophages.

claim: DNA-PK activation upon Mtb infection does not influence the survival of the pathogen
source: It is evident that addition of DNA-PK-I or ATR-I did not alter the CFUs, suggesting that even though DNA-PK seems to be activated upon Mtb infection, it does not influence the survival of the pathogen (Figure 6c and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effect of DNA-PK-I on CFUs despite DNA-PKcs activation shown in Figure 6a and 6c.

claim: H37Rv infection of peritoneal macrophages results in activation of Akt (phosphorylation at S473)
source: Western blot analysis showed that treatment with either ATM-I or Akt-I inhibited the activation of ATM and Akt, respectively (Figure 6e).
evidence: Figure 6d shows pAkt(S473) in Rv infected peritoneal macrophages at 4, 24, and 48 hr.

claim: Treatment with ATM inhibitor results in reduced activation of Akt in H37Rv infected cells
source: While treatment of cells with ATM-I resulted in reduced activation of Akt, addition of Akt-I did not impact activation of ATM, suggesting that ATM activation is upstream of Akt activation (Figure 6e).
evidence: Figure 6e shows reduced pAkt in Rv+ATM-I treated cells compared to Rv alone.

claim: Addition of Akt inhibitor does not impact activation of ATM in H37Rv infected cells
source: While treatment of cells with ATM-I resulted in reduced activation of Akt, addition of Akt-I did not impact activation of ATM, suggesting that ATM activation is upstream of Akt activation (Figure 6e).
evidence: Figure 6e shows similar pATM levels in Rv and Rv+Akt-I treated cells.

claim: ATM activation is upstream of Akt activation in H37Rv infected cells
source: While treatment of cells with ATM-I resulted in reduced activation of Akt, addition of Akt-I did not impact activation of ATM, suggesting that ATM activation is upstream of Akt activation (Figure 6e).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ATM-I reduces Akt activation but Akt-I does not affect ATM activation, as shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Administration of Akt inhibitor alone or in combination with ATM inhibitor significantly reduces intracellular survival of Mtb
source: Data suggests that administration of Akt inhibitor (Akt-I) alone or in combination with ATM-I significantly reduced the intracellular survival of Mtb (Figure 6f).
evidence: Figure 6f shows reduced CFUs in Rv+Akt-I and Rv+ATM-I+Akt-I treated peritoneal macrophages compared to Rv alone.

claim: Treatment with combination of ATM-I + Akt-I shows survival defects similar to Akt-I alone, indicating that ATM mediated signals are channeling through Akt
source: Treatment with a combination of ATM-I + Akt-I showed survival defects similar to Akt-I alone indicating that ATM mediated signals are channeling through Akt (Figure 6f and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 6f shows similar CFU reduction in Rv+Akt-I and Rv+ATM-I+Akt-I treated cells, suggesting no additive effect.

claim: The impact of Akt inhibitor on the survival of H37Rv is higher compared with ATM inhibitor
source: Interestingly, the impact of Akt inhibitor on the survival of Rv was higher compared with ATM-I (Figure 6f; Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 6f shows greater CFU reduction with Akt-I compared to ATM-I.

claim: Other signaling pathways besides ATM could be involved in activating Akt during Mtb infection
source: Moreover, while the addition of ATM-I decreased activation of Akt, the reduction with Akt-I was higher, suggesting that other signaling pathways could also be involved in activating Akt (Figure 6e).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Akt-I has a greater effect on Mtb survival than ATM-I, and that ATM-I only partially reduces Akt activation, as shown in Figure 6e-f.

claim: Addition of ATM-I or Akt-I or ATM-I + Akt-I decreases the percent live population in H37Rv-infected cells
source: While the addition of inhibitors did not impact the percent live cells (Figure 6g; top panel and Figure 6—source data 1) in UI, their presence decreased the percent live population in Rv-infected cells (Figure 6g; top panel and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 6g top panel shows decreased percentage of live cells in Rv+ATM-I, Rv+Akt-I, and Rv+ATM-I+Akt-I compared to Rv alone.

claim: Addition of ATM-I or Akt-I or ATM-I + Akt-I increases early and late apoptotic cells in H37Rv-infected cells
source: We observed concomitant increase in the early and late apoptotic cells in the presence of ATM-I or Akt-I or ATM-I + Akt-I (Figure 6g; bottom panel and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 6g bottom panel shows increased percentage of early and late apoptotic cells in Rv+ATM-I, Rv+Akt-I, and Rv+ATM-I+Akt-I compared to Rv alone.

claim: H37Rv inflicts DSBs to activate ATM which in turn activates Akt resulting in anti-apoptotic and pro-survival signals that favor Mtb survival
source: Thus, the data suggests that Rv inflicts DSBs to activate ATM which in turn activates Akt resulting in anti-apoptotic and pro-survival signals which favors Mtb survival (Figure 7g).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the data in Figures 5 and 6, and is depicted in the model in Figure 7g.

claim: Mtb establishes chronic infection in mouse lungs at 56 days post-infection with significant bacillary load
source: We observed appearance of granulomatous lesions and significant bacillary load at 56 days p.i suggesting that Mtb has established chronic infection in the lungs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Figure 7a shows CFU data at day 1 and day 56, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1a shows images of infected lungs with lesions.

claim: Lungs of H37Rv infected mice show significantly elevated levels of γH2AX, pATM, pChk2 and pAkt at 56 days post-infection
source: While the levels of γH2AX, pATM, pChk2, and pAkt was negligible in the uninfected mice lungs, we observed significantly elevated levels of γH2AX, pATM, pChk2 and pAkt in the lungs of Rv infected mice, suggesting that Mtb infection produces sustained DSBs and Akt mediated proliferation (Figure 7b and Figure 7—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Figure 7b shows western blots with elevated γH2AX, pATM, pChk2, and pAkt in lung lysates from Rv infected mice compared to uninfected controls.

claim: Mtb infection produces sustained DSBs in mouse lungs during chronic infection
source: While the levels of γH2AX, pATM, pChk2, and pAkt was negligible in the uninfected mice lungs, we observed significantly elevated levels of γH2AX, pATM, pChk2 and pAkt in the lungs of Rv infected mice, suggesting that Mtb infection produces sustained DSBs and Akt mediated proliferation (Figure 7b and Figure 7—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is inferred from the elevated γH2AX and pATM levels in infected mouse lungs shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Increased γH2AX levels are observed in spleen lysates of H37Rv infected mice
source: In a similar vein, we also observed increased levels of γH2AX in the lysates obtained from spleen of infected mice (Figure 7b; bottom panels).
evidence: Figure 7b bottom panel shows elevated γH2AX in spleen lysates from Rv infected mice.

claim: H37Rv disseminates from lungs to spleen by 56 days post-infection
source: CFUs in spleen after 56 days of infection suggests dissemination of Rv from lungs (Figure 7a).
evidence: Figure 7a shows CFUs in spleen at day 56 post-infection.

claim: Pathogenic Mtb induces genotoxicity both ex vivo and in vivo resulting in deleterious DSBs in the host genome
source: Collectively the results suggest that pathogenic Mtb induces genotoxicity both ex vivo and in vivo resulting in deleterious DSBs in the host genome.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the ex vivo data in Figures 1-6 and in vivo data in Figure 7a-b.

claim: Treatment of H37Rv infected peritoneal macrophages with ATM-I + INH decreases pathogen survival by ~11 fold
source: Notably, treatment of Rv infected cells with ATM-I + INH decreased the pathogen survival by ~11 fold.
evidence: Figure 7c shows CFU data demonstrating ~11 fold reduction with ATM-I+INH treatment compared to untreated Rv.

claim: Treatment of H37Rv infected peritoneal macrophages with INH alone decreases pathogen survival by ~4 fold
source: The treatment of Rv infected cells with ATM-I or INH alone decreased the survival of pathogen by ~2 or 4-fold, respectively (Figure 7c and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 7c shows CFU data demonstrating ~4 fold reduction with INH treatment alone.

claim: Treatment of H37Rv infected peritoneal macrophages with ATM-I alone decreases pathogen survival by ~2 fold
source: The treatment of Rv infected cells with ATM-I or INH alone decreased the survival of pathogen by ~2 or 4-fold, respectively (Figure 7c and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 7c shows CFU data demonstrating ~2 fold reduction with ATM-I treatment alone.

claim: Treatment with INH alone results in ~1 log fold reduction in Mtb load in mouse lungs
source: While treatment with INH alone resulted ~1 log fold reduction in the Mtb load, treatment with ATM-I alone did not show any difference.
evidence: Figure 7e shows CFU data in mouse lungs with ~1 log reduction in INH treated group compared to Rv.

claim: Treatment with ATM-I alone does not show difference in Mtb load in mouse lungs
source: While treatment with INH alone resulted ~1 log fold reduction in the Mtb load, treatment with ATM-I alone did not show any difference.
evidence: Figure 7e shows similar CFUs in Rv and Rv+ATM-I groups in mouse lungs.

claim: Combination of ATM-I + INH treatment results in ~1 log fold better clearance compared with INH treatment alone in mouse lungs
source: Notably, combination of ATM-I + INH treatment resulted in ~1 log fold better clearance compared with INH treatment alone (Figure 7e and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: Figure 7e shows CFU data in mouse lungs with ~1 log better reduction in INH+ATM-I group compared to INH alone.

claim: The impact of ATM-I+INH treatment compared with INH treatment alone is more evident in the spleen
source: The impact of ATM-I+INH treatment compared with INH treatment alone was more evident in the spleen (Figure 7f and Figure 7—source data 1), suggesting combined therapy might have compromised dissemination of the pathogen.
evidence: Figure 7f shows greater CFU reduction in spleen with INH+ATM-I treatment compared to INH alone.

claim: Combined ATM-I+INH therapy might have compromised dissemination of Mtb from lungs to spleen
source: The impact of ATM-I+INH treatment compared with INH treatment alone was more evident in the spleen (Figure 7f and Figure 7—source data 1), suggesting combined therapy might have compromised dissemination of the pathogen.
evidence: This is inferred from the greater effect of combination therapy in spleen compared to lungs, as shown in Figure 7f.

claim: ATM inhibitor is a potential candidate for host directed therapy against tuberculosis
source: Taken together, we propose that ATM inhibitor is a potential candidate for HDT.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing enhanced Mtb clearance with ATM-I+INH combination in both ex vivo (Figure 7c) and in vivo (Figure 7e-f) models.

claim: H37Ra is considered an attenuated, avirulent strain of Mtb based on reduced survival under anaerobic conditions and inability to produce persistent infection in mice and guinea pigs
source: Based on its characteristics such as reduced survival under anaerobic conditions, inability to produce persistent infection in mice and guinea pigs, Ra is considered as attenuated, avirulent strain of Mtb (Alsaadi and Smith, 1973; North and Izzo, 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to Alsaadi and Smith, 1973 and North and Izzo, 1993.

claim: RvΔsecA2 strongly induces markers of apoptosis in both human and murine macrophages
source: Moreover, a previous study (Hinchey et al., 2007) showed that RvΔsecA2 strongly induced markers of apoptosis in both human and murine macrophages suggesting a critical role played by SecA2 secretome in preventing apoptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation to Hinchey et al., 2007.

claim: SecA2 secretome plays a critical role in preventing apoptosis in Mtb infected cells
source: Moreover, a previous study (Hinchey et al., 2007) showed that RvΔsecA2 strongly induced markers of apoptosis in both human and murine macrophages suggesting a critical role played by SecA2 secretome in preventing apoptosis.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited study showing increased apoptosis with RvΔsecA2.

claim: Following DSBs, ATM-dependent phosphorylation of ~700 substrates regulates multitude of cellular processes such as cell cycle and cellular differentiation
source: High-throughput study revealed that following DSBs, ATM-dependent phosphorylation of ~700 substrates regulate multitude of cellular processes such as cell cycle, cellular differentiation etc., emphasizing its global regulatory role.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion, likely referring to established knowledge from high-throughput studies.

claim: DDR crosstalks with the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt pathway to elicit cell survival signals
source: Importantly, DDR was suggested to crosstalk with the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt pathway to elicit cell survival signals, which is also supported by data that demonstrated ATM-dependent phosphorylation of Akt at S473 (Khalil et al., 2011; Matsuoka et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to Khalil et al., 2011 and Matsuoka et al., 2007.

claim: ATM-dependent phosphorylation of Akt at S473 has been demonstrated
source: Importantly, DDR was suggested to crosstalk with the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt pathway to elicit cell survival signals, which is also supported by data that demonstrated ATM-dependent phosphorylation of Akt at S473 (Khalil et al., 2011; Matsuoka et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to Khalil et al., 2011 and Matsuoka et al., 2007.

claim: Inhibiting Akt diminishes Mtb survival inside host cells
source: Previous reports suggested that inhibiting Akt diminished Mtb survival inside host cells and proposed it to be a novel target for host directed therapy (Kuijl et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation to Kuijl et al., 2007.

claim: Apoptotic death is considered advantageous for the host as it results in elimination of Mtb pathogen
source: Apoptotic death is considered to be advantageous for the host as it results in the elimination of pathogen (Fratazzi et al., 1999; Gan et al., 2008; Molloy et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to Fratazzi et al., 1999, Gan et al., 2008, and Molloy et al., 1994.

claim: Induction of non-apoptotic death of host cells is beneficial for Mtb bacilli as it fails to eliminate the pathogen
source: Induction of non-apoptotic death of the host cells is beneficial for the bacilli as it fails to eliminate the pathogen (Dobos et al., 2000; Keane et al., 2000; Lee and Paull, 2005; Martin et al., 2012; Park et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to multiple studies.

claim: Internalization of Mtb aggregates by host cells results in killing of the host through non-apoptotic pathway
source: Recently, it was reported that internalization of Mtb aggregates by the host cell results in killing of the host and there was a direct correlation between the size of aggregates and cell death. However, the death in such cases was through non-apoptotic pathway (Mahamed et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation to Mahamed et al., 2017.

claim: There is a direct correlation between the size of Mtb aggregates and host cell death
source: Recently, it was reported that internalization of Mtb aggregates by the host cell results in killing of the host and there was a direct correlation between the size of aggregates and cell death. However, the death in such cases was through non-apoptotic pathway (Mahamed et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation to Mahamed et al., 2017.

claim: Salmonella typhimurium and Coxiella burnetii get survival advantage through Akt activation
source: These results are in line with the previous findings, wherein bacterial pathogens such as Salmonella typhimurium and Coxiella burnetii have been shown to get survival advantage through Akt activation (Kuijl et al., 2007; Voth and Heinzen, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to Kuijl et al., 2007 and Voth and Heinzen, 2009.

claim: Mtb mediated DNA damage is not ROS-dependent
source: In agreement with this, addition of N-acetyl cysteine (NAC), a scavenger of ROS, to the infected cells did not alter the γH2AX, suggesting that DNA damage is not mediated through ROS (Figure 7—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Figure 7—figure supplement 1c shows that NAC treatment does not reduce γH2AX levels in Rv infected cells.

claim: Secretion of 37 proteins including Mce1, Mce4 family and multiple solute binding lipoproteins is dependent on the SecA2 pathway
source: Mass spectrometry-based study has identified the secretion of 37 proteins, including Mce1, Mce4 family and multiple solute binding lipoproteins to be dependent on the SecA2 pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion, referring to mass spectrometry studies.

claim: Secretion of protein kinase G (PknG), superoxide dismutase (SodA) and phosphatase SapM proteins is through SecA2 pathway
source: In addition to these, secretion of protein kinase G (PknG), superoxide dismutase (SodA) and phosphatase SapM proteins are also through SecA2 pathway (Feltcher et al., 2015; Miller et al., 2017; Sullivan et al., 2012; Zulauf et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to multiple studies.

claim: One or more lipoproteins secreted through the SecA2 pathway could be critical for genotoxicity
source: As polyketides and lipids from mycobacteria were suggested to be cyclomodulins; therefore, we speculate that one or more lipoproteins secreted through the SecA2 pathway could be critical for genotoxicity (Cumming et al., 2017; George et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the Discussion with citations to Cumming et al., 2017 and George et al., 1998.

claim: Mice lacking p47 and gp91 subunit of NADPH oxidase (gp91phox-/-) are susceptible to Mtb as macrophages fail to generate ROS
source: Mice lacking p47 and gp91 subunit of NADPH oxidase (gp91phox-/-) are susceptible to Mtb as the macrophages in these mice fail to generate ROS (Cooper et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation to Cooper et al., 2000.

claim: SodAMtb secreted through SecA2 pathway plays an important role in detoxification of ROS generated inside the host
source: SodAMtb, which is secreted through SecA2 pathway plays an important role in detoxification of ROS generated inside the host thus partially neutralizing the anti-microbial property of ROS (Chan et al., 1992; Lau et al., 1998; Piddington et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to Chan et al., 1992, Lau et al., 1998, and Piddington et al., 2001.

claim: In RvΔSecA2 mutant, SodAMtb secretion is expected to be compromised
source: In RvΔSecA2 mutant SodAMtb secretion is expected to be compromised and hence one would expect higher levels of host ROS upon infection.
evidence: This is inferred from the knowledge that SodA is secreted via SecA2 pathway, stated in the Discussion.

claim: The fact that RvΔSecA2 mutant fails to inflict DSBs suggests that Mtb mediated damage is unlikely to be ROS-dependent
source: The fact that RvΔSecA2 mutant fails to inflict DSBs suggest that Mtb mediated damage is unlikely to be ROS-dependent.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RvΔSecA2 does not cause DSBs despite potentially higher ROS levels, as discussed in the text.
